title: tt-bio at 512 residues: Tenstorrent against NVIDIA
subtitle: Five structure-prediction models, one fixture, measured wall-clock.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, throughput per dollar and every ratio are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and the assumptions block.
A cell with no measurement gets status 'pending' or 'blocked' and a reason. Do not fill it with an estimate.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, synthetic MSA of exactly 35 sequences.
scope.protocol: Warm folds only. The cold fold is discarded explicitly on both sides. Tenstorrent runs are benchlocked (exclusive host) and alternate their arms inside one process, so both arms of a comparison share one noise floor; every Tenstorrent cell states that A/A floor. GPU runs quote a median of n=3.

badges.measured: Measured on the hardware named, on this fixture.
badges.derived: Computed from a measured number plus a stated assumption. The assumption is on the chart.

options.label: one fold at a time
options.detail: What both sides were measured at. No MPS on the GPU, no multi-process sharing of a Tenstorrent chip (tt-bio takes an flock before opening a device, so one process per chip is enforced).

options.label: GPU with MPS, 2.0x
options.detail: The H200's measured MPS ceiling at 298 aa: one fold already puts it at 68.1 % utilization, so MPS buys 2.00x before saturating. At 117 aa, where one fold leaves the GPU at 33.5 %, MPS bought 6.53x. The 512 aa value is not measured. Applied to the NVIDIA servers only; the Tenstorrent side has no equivalent lever measured at this size.

concurrency.note: Charts 1 and 4 read this. Chart 3 does not: it is a latency question.

assumptions.throughput_formula: predictions per hour = 3600 / s_per_fold * accelerators * scaling_efficiency * concurrency

galaxy_scaling.kind: assumption carried from a different generation
galaxy_scaling.detail: 27.8x of 32 chips, measured on a Wormhole Galaxy folding Protenix-v2. Whether it transfers to a Blackhole Galaxy is unknown and untested. The dominant cost is host CPU sync per fold, roughly 1.007 cores, independent of card generation; a faster chip amortizes that over a shorter fold, so the Blackhole figure could be lower rather than equal.

gpu_scaling.detail: 8 GPUs folding independent targets are assumed to scale perfectly. No multi-GPU fanout was measured. This favours NVIDIA.

not_applied: Diffusion-sample batching. Both stacks have it and the H200 uses it better: 4 samples cost the H200 4 % more wall time and a p150a 49 % more, measured at 117 aa. It is left off both sides because 4 samples of one target are 4 poses, not 4 answers.
tt-bio's multi-prediction batching, measured at 1.72x for batch 8, is not applied to the Tenstorrent bars.
Power. The Galaxy Blackhole and an 8-GPU HGX node have very different power envelopes and neither was measured here.

caveats: Rows are not a cross-model ranking. Boltz-2 and OpenFold3 do 3 recycles where Protenix-v2, OpenDDE and ESMFold2 do 10, because that is what each ships. Compare a model to itself across hardware, not to another model.
The B200 is not uniformly faster than the H200 here. It wins ESMFold2 by 24.7 % and loses Boltz-2 by 10.2 % and OpenFold3 by 15.9 %. Its node also had a weaker host, 24 vCPU against 28.
Accuracy is not compared on this page. Each stack ran its own shipped defaults and every run was sanity-checked against its own plDDT, but the models differ and the numbers here are wall-clock only.
The GPU numbers come from single rented nodes, not from a DGX. The server figures multiply one measured GPU by 8 and assume a DGX or HGX node reaches the same per-GPU fold time.
The Tenstorrent cards measured here report an 11x10 compute grid, 110 cores. Other Blackhole hosts report 13x10.

OpenFold3's 1.8981x is hoisting, not a new kernel. The diffusion conditioning branch, the encoder pair update and the DiT pair bias are computed once per rollout instead of 200 times, which is why the answer does not change. Routing its fp32-softmax triangle attention through the fused SDPA kernel was tried separately and rejected: it moved the structure by 27.3 A.
